review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–90). It has two declarations. `countable_potentialIso_iff_iso` is a thin wrapper around `PotentialIso.nonempty_equiv_of_cg`. All the repetition is inside the single proof of `nonempty_equiv_of_cg`. There are three symmetric pairs: the inl/inr cofinal sets in `D`, `hXdom`/`hYcod`, and `hdom`/`hcod`. Each pair is a short block of 3–6 lines, and each differs in the direction (dom vs cod) and in the hypotheses used (`hforth` vs `hback`, `PartialEquiv.dom_le_dom` vs `PartialEquiv.cod_le_cod`). The rubric asks for nontrivial reasoning repeated across at least two proofs. It says short calculations, routine unfolding, and moving duplicated branches into a helper are insufficient. These symmetric branches inside one proof fall under that exclusion. A shared helper would need to abstract over dom/cod and forth/back, and that would likely cost more than it saves. I did not search other files for a second proof that repeats the argument. I'm fairly confident nothing in this file justifies a finding.
